// Puzzle data for Spot, the daily spot the difference game (owner, 2026-11-12).
// Imported ONLY by the server pages (app/spot/page.js and, for the kids copy,
// app/kids/kids-spot-boards.js), which filter live<=today, so a future photo
// name and its answer key never reach a browser.
//
// GENERATED by scripts/spot/export.py from the op lists in scripts/spot/boards.py
// (built by scripts/spot/spotkit.py). Never hand-edit a row, and never rebuild a
// board that has gone live: append days only. scripts/verify-spot.mjs checks
// every row against the photo files themselves.
//
// THE GAME. Two copies of one photograph, the second altered in `diffs` places
// (seven on every board so far). The player taps either copy where they differ.
// Score is the number found; then fewest misses (a wrong tap is one, a hint is
// two); then the clock. No Sunday Edition: every day is seven differences.
//
// THE PHOTOS are past Jig photographs (Wikimedia Commons featured pictures, all
// CC BY or CC BY-SA, which allow altered copies with credit). `jig` is the Jig
// board the photo came from, and `name`, `lic`, `by` are that row's own credit,
// printed under the board with a note that the second copy is altered. A photo
// is used here only AFTER its Jig day, so Spot never shows tomorrow's jigsaw.
//
// Fields. img: the opaque file stem, public/spot/<img>-a.jpg (original) and
// <img>-b.jpg (altered), both `w` by `h`. diffs: [{ x, y: the centre as a
// fraction of width and height; rx, ry: the hit ellipse's radii, BOTH as a
// fraction of the WIDTH; t: what changed, in plain words, printed once found }].
//
// WHAT MAKES A BOARD GOOD (the authoring rules, held by the verifier where it can):
//   1. Every difference is visible at 1x on a phone: no radius under 0.021.
//   2. Aim for a mix: recolors (the easy ones), removals, an added object and at
//      least one small or subtle change. A photo with nothing clean to remove
//      may run all recolors (Lviv, Masks), never two such days in a row.
//   3. A removal takes its reflection or shadow with it.
//   4. Nothing changes outside a listed difference (the grid check).
//   5. Labels say what changed in the SECOND copy, US spelling, no em dash.
